decisions.rationale: Klefki+Gengar lead: Prankster TWave Swampert-Mega for speed control; Gengar-Mega Thunderbolt breaks Pelipper Focus Sash (4x) + Shadow Tag traps. If Swampert Protects, Klefki sets Reflect. KO Pelipper next turn to remove rain→no Swift Swim. Paralyzed Swampert outsped by all. Back: Conkeldurr (CC Swampert/Archaludon, Mach Punch Heliolisk) + Corviknight (Tailwind, Brave Bird Tsareena, Ground immunity). Leave Gyarados (bad rain) and Mamoswine (EQ hits ally, QM blocks priority).
decisions.notebook: G2 plan: Klefki+Gengar lead into rain core. Key calcs: Swampert-Mega HH possible OHKO on Gengar-Mega (91-209%) and Klefki (85-192%); Reflect halves these. Gengar-Mega Tbolt guaranteed >100% on Pelipper but Focus Sash→1 HP. Conkeldurr CC 47-97% on Swampert-Mega (2HKO), 88-179% on Archaludon (poss OHKO). Mach Punch 60-150% on Heliolisk (poss OHKO w/ chip). Corviknight immune to HH (Flying), Liquidation 42-88% (survives), Brave Bird 55-131% on Tsareena (poss OHKO). Queenly Majesty blocks Prankster TWave on Tsareena's side—must handle Tsareena before relying on priority. Without rain, Swampert-Mega 90-122 Spe; paralyzed 45-61, outsped by entire team. Opponent Protects predictably when threatened—use this to set Reflect/TWave safely. Win condition: remove Pelipper (end rain) + paralyze Swampert → Conkeldurr CC cleans up. Corviknight Tailwind as backup speed control. Gengar Shadow Tag prevents Pelipper swap at 1 HP.

decisions.rationale: Leading Swampert and Pelipper immediately sets Rain to activate Swift Swim on Mega Swampert, allowing it to outspeed Mega Gengar and pressure the opponent's entire team. Archaludon in the back gains instant Electro Shot turns in Rain, while Tsareena provides Queenly Majesty to block priority moves such as Conkeldurr's Mach Punch, Mamoswine's Ice Shard, and Klefki's Prankster status.

Prankster TWave paralyzes Swampert before it moves (priority). Switching Gengar to Corviknight preserves Gengar-Mega for later Shadow Tag while bringing in Flying-type immunity to Swampert's HH. If Swampert targeted Gengar (likely), HH fails. Next turn: Corviknight Tailwind + Klefki Reflect for speed/defense control. Gengar-Mega can't survive HH even with Reflect (99-137%), so keeping it safe is critical.
decisions.notebook: G2 plan updated: Gengar-Mega CANNOT survive Swampert-Mega HH even with Reflect (99.3-137.2%). Without Reflect it's guaranteed OHKO (148.9-205.8%). Must keep Gengar-Mega off the field vs Swampert-Mega unless Swampert is paralyzed AND rain is gone (no Swift Swim). Win path: (1) TWave Swampert done T1, (2) bring Gengar-Mega in later with Tailwind up to trap+KO Pelipper (Tbolt 4x SE, Sash saves at 1HP, need 2 hits), (3) rain ends when Pelipper faints, Swampert-Mega paralyzed+no Swift Swim=45-61 Spe, (4) Conkeldurr CC cleans up. Corviknight is HH-immune (Flying) and key switch-in for Swampert. Pelipper likely Protects when threatened by Tbolt—don't waste Gengar-Mega on predicted Protects. Tailwind from Corviknight makes Gengar-Mega 400 Spe, outspeeding everything.

decisions.rationale: Mega Swampert with Swift Swim under Rain reaches 244 Speed, outspeeding Timid Mega Gengar (max 200 Speed). High Horsepower deals 151.1–177.8% to Mega Gengar, guaranteeing an OHKO before it can act or use Thunderbolt/Sludge Bomb. Pelipper sets up Tailwind to guarantee total speed control and turn-order dominance for the team even if Gengar Protects or weather changes.
decisions.notebook: Swampert + Pelipper lead against Mega Gengar + Klefki. Mega Swampert in Rain reaches 244 Speed, outspeeding Timid Mega Gengar (200 max) and OHKOing with High Horsepower.

decisions.rationale: Klefki Protect avoids guaranteed OHKO from Swampert HH (109.8-153.7%). Corviknight sets Tailwind for future speed control. Corviknight is HH-immune so even if predicted, only eats Ice Punch (20.5-28.8%). Pelipper is NVE into both Steel-types. Stalls opp Tailwind (3→2) and rain (4→3). Conkeldurr switch-in is unsafe: Pelipper Hurricane is SE 2x into Fighting (57.5-173.3%, possible OHKO). Must stall until rain+Swift Swim expire.
decisions.notebook: Swampert-Mega IMMUNE to TWave (Ground-type). Original para plan dead. HH damage: Klefki 109.8-153.7% (guaranteed OHKO), with Reflect 73.2-102.4% (possible OHKO, too risky), Conkeldurr 29.7-76.7% (survives), Corviknight immune (0x). Pelipper Hurricane: Klefki 15.9-23.8% NVE, Conkeldurr 57.5-173.3% SE 2x (possible OHKO!), Corviknight NVE. Conkeldurr CANNOT safely switch in while Pelipper can Hurricane it. Corviknight Brave Bird Swampert-Mega 21.7-38.3% chip. Swampert Ice Punch Corviknight 20.5-28.8%. New win path: stall with Klefki Protect + Corviknight Tailwind/Brave Bird until rain (4 turns) and opp Tailwind (3 turns) expire. Without rain+Swift Swim+Tailwind, Swampert-Mega drops to 45-61 Spe, outsped by everything with my Tailwind. Bring Conkeldurr in only when Pelipper is gone or predicted to Protect. Gengar-Mega still cannot enter vs Swampert-Mega. Tsareena HJK is SE vs Steel—watch for that switch-in.

decisions.rationale: Swampert outspeeds everything under Swift Swim and Tailwind. High Horsepower + Hydro Pump double-target into Klefki ensures a KO on Klefki even if it sets up Reflect (Hydro Pump bypasses Reflect as a special attack) or survives a solo hit, removing Prankster status and screen setup. Corviknight poses no immediate threat to either active slot.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 (Score: p1 0, p2 1). Swampert + Pelipper lead against Mega Gengar + Klefki. Turn 1 Klefki used T-Wave into Swampert (immune). Swampert High Horsepower into Corviknight switch-in (immune). Swampert in Rain + Tailwind reaches 376 Speed.

decisions.rationale: Klefki TWave Pelipper (Prankster priority) paralyzes Pelipper before dying to Swampert HH—permanent speed cripple is huge. Corviknight Brave Bird chips Swampert 20-43% while staying safe (immune to HH, NVE from Pelipper). Next turn: bring Gengar-Mega, Thunderbolt Pelipper to 1HP (Sash), then finish it. Stall Swampert after rain/Tailwind expire.
decisions.notebook: TWave Pelipper confirmed legal (Water/Flying not Electric-immune). Prankster priority ensures TWave lands before Klefki dies to HH. Gengar-Mega Thunderbolt guaranteed OHKOs Pelipper (117-326%) but Focus Sash saves at 1HP—need one more hit to finish. Gengar-Mega fragile: Pelipper Hydro Pump 43.7-127.4% possible OHKO, Swampert Liquidation 56.3-156.3% possible OHKO, Ice Punch 22.2-61.5% survivable. Bring Gengar in only when Swampert predicted to use HH (Gengar immune to Ground). Conkeldurr Mach Punch vs Pelipper = 0.25x (Fighting vs Water/Flying), useless for killing Pelipper. Win path: paralyze Pelipper → Gengar-Mega Thunderbolt to 1HP → finish Pelipper → stall Swampert with Corviknight Brave Bird chip (20-43% per hit) until rain (3 turns) and opp Tailwind (2 turns) expire. Swampert drops to 45-61 Spe without Swift Swim+Tailwind, outsped by everything. Corviknight immune to HH (Ground), NVE from Pelipper (Flying0.25x, Water 0.5x)—ideal staller. Keep Corviknight healthy as primary staller.

decisions.rationale: Conkeldurr is the safer switch-in. It survives Swampert HH (29.7-76.7%, cannot OHKO) and has better survival odds vs Liquidation (39.6-102.2%) than Gengar-Mega (56.3-156.3%). Close Combat can KO Swampert at 62% HP (46.9-96.6%). Knock Off removes Pelipper's Focus Sash (22.8-50.4%). Conkeldurr (134 w/Tailwind) outspeeds paralyzed Pelipper (85-117). Gengar kept in reserve for when Swampert loses Swift Swim+Tailwind after rain expires. Corviknight must stay healthy—Pelipper Hydro Pump is neutral 1x and can KO at 47%.
decisions.notebook: CRITICAL CORRECTION: Water vs Corviknight (Flying/Steel) is NEUTRAL 1x, NOT NVE 0.5x as previously noted. Pelipper Hydro Pump does 38.5-57.6% to Corviknight—can KO at current 47% HP. Hurricane is 0.25x NVE (correct). Swampert HH vs Conkeldurr: 29.7-76.7% (survivable). Swampert Liquidation vs Conkeldurr: 39.6-102.2% (possible OHKO but lower floor than Gengar). Conkeldurr Close Combat vs Swampert-Mega: 46.9-96.6%—can KO at 62% HP on high rolls. Conkeldurr Knock Off vs Pelipper: 22.8-50.4% + removes Focus Sash (Sash doesn't activate since damage <100%). Conkeldurr (134 w/Tailwind) outspeeds paralyzed Pelipper (85-117). Swampert (360-488) outspeeds everything. Speed order next turn: Swampert > Conkeldurr > Pelipper. Plan: Turn 4 Conkeldurr Knock Off Pelipper Sash + Corviknight Brave Bird/Protect Swampert. Bring Gengar-Mega later when rain (3T) + opp Tailwind (2T) expire—Swampert drops to 45-61 Spe, outsped by Gengar-Mega (165-200). Shadow Tag then traps safely. Win path: remove Pelipper Sash → kill Pelipper → stall Swampert with Corviknight + Conkeldurr chip until speed drops → bring Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Swampert outspeeds everything under Rain and Tailwind. High Horsepower deals 92.7-174.2% to Klefki, while Pelipper's Rain-boosted Hydro Pump deals 51.2-98.5% (unaffected by Reflect). Doubling Klefki guarantees its KO even through Prankster Reflect or low damage rolls. Klefki's Protect used on Turn 2 has a 67% chance to fail if attempted again. Corviknight's Brave Bird cannot OHKO Pelipper.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent leads Klefki + Corviknight. Rain + Tailwind active. Klefki used Protect T2 (success rate reduced T3). Corviknight cannot OHKO Pelipper with Brave Bird (45.2-69.6%). Swampert outspeeds entire opposing side in Rain + Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Knock Off removes Pelipper Focus Sash (critical win con). Corviknight Protects—safe from Hydro Pump/Liquidation KO at 47%. Conkeldurr at 100% best survives a hit. If Swampert Protects expecting Close Combat, we still remove Sash. Next turn opp Tailwind expires; we outspeed paralyzed Pelipper to KO it. Rain ends after T5; T6 Gengar-Mega outspeeds Swampert for Shadow Tag.
decisions.notebook: Win path: remove Pelipper Sash → KO Pelipper → rain expires → Swampert loses Swift Swim → Gengar-Mega (165-200) outspeeds Swampert (90-122) for Shadow Tag trap. Speed timeline: T4 Swampert 360-488 > Corviknight 174 > Conkeldurr 134 > para Pelipper 85-117. T5 (opp TWind gone, rain 1T left): Swampert 180-244 > Corviknight 174 > Conkeldurr 134 > para Pelipper 42-58. T6 (no rain/TWind): Gengar-Mega 165-200 > Swampert 90-122. Pelipper Hurricane OHKOs Conkeldurr (87.7-131.1%). Swampert HH vs Conkeldurr 29.7-65.1%. Close Combat vs Swampert 39.1-82.9% from 62%. Brave Bird vs Swampert 20.3-42.9%. Hydro Pump vs Corviknight 38.5-57.6% (KO at 47%). Liquidation vs Corviknight 35.1-48.8% (KO at 47%). Knock Off vs Pelipper 22.8-50.4% + removes Sash. Conkeldurr outspeeds para Pelipper. Key: never let Conkeldurr take HH+Hurricane same turn. Bring Gengar-Mega T6 when rain expires.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Swampert outspeeds Corviknight in Rain+Tailwind (376 Speed). Rain-boosted Liquidation targets Corviknight (46% HP) for 41-88.4% damage to clear or heavily chip it before it can move. Pelipper's 100% accurate Rain Hurricane into Conkeldurr deals 63.2-147.8% super-effective damage. Conkeldurr's Mach Punch (+1 priority) deals only 22.9-33.1% to Swampert, allowing Swampert to comfortably survive even if both foes attack it.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent leads Klefki + Corviknight; brought Conkeldurr in back. Klefki fainted T3 to Swampert High Horsepower. Swampert in Rain+Tailwind reaches 376 Speed, outspeeding entire opposing team. Conkeldurr Mach Punch does 22.9-33.1% to Swampert. Corviknight Brave Bird does 32.6-49.7% to Swampert. Pelipper Rain Hurricane into Conkeldurr deals 63.2-147.8%.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve Gengar for Shadow Tag active T6 (prevents opp switches). Protect blocks Swampert's likely HH (2x SE, 82-233% possible OHKO). Corviknight Brave Birds Swampert (20-55%), chipping to 7-42% for T6 Shadow Ball KO (24-58%). T6: no rain, Shadow Tag traps both foes, Gengar-Mega outspeeds Swampert. Thunderbolt KOs Pelipper (28%), then Shadow Ball finishes Swampert. Risk: if Swampert targets Corviknight instead, Liquidation could KO at 53%, but Swampert is incentivized to hit Gengar (prevents Shadow Tag).
decisions.notebook: Game 2 T5 plan: Mega Evolved Gengar T5 for Shadow Tag on T6. Tailwind fails if already active—must wait for expiry before re-using. T6 speed (no rain/TW): Gengar-Mega 165-200 > Swampert 90-122 > Corviknight 87 > para Pelipper 42-58. Shadow Ball vs Swampert-Mega: 24-58% (KO if Swampert below ~40%). Thunderbolt guaranteed KOs Pelipper at 28%. Swampert HH vs Gengar-Mega: 83-233% possible OHKO—always Protect Gengar when Swampert can hit it. Pelipper Hydro Pump vs Corviknight at 53%: 39-109% possible KO. Brave Bird vs Swampert: 20-55% chip. Series score p1 0, p2 1—must win G2 and G3. Only Gengar+Corviknight remain (Klefki, Conkeldurr fainted). Win path: Shadow Tag trap + outspeed + pick off foes one by one.

decisions.rationale: Opponent's Tailwind has 1 turn left. A double-target from Gengar (Shadow Ball) and Corviknight (Brave Bird) threatens a KO on Swampert before it acts. Protecting Swampert completely neutralizes this threat while opponent's Tailwind expires. Switching Pelipper to Archaludon safely preserves Pelipper while Archaludon comfortably eats any move directed at slot b thanks to its typing and bulk, positioning us to dominate Turn 6.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent brought Klefki + Corviknight + Conkeldurr + Gengar. Klefki fainted T3, Conkeldurr fainted T4. Opponent Gengar item Gengarite, moves: Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Thunderbolt, Protect. Corviknight item Leftovers, moves: Brave Bird, Tailwind, U-turn, Protect. Swampert in Rain outspeeds opponent's entire unboosted team. Opponent Tailwind expires after T5.

decisions.rationale: Desperate spot: Swampert HH guaranteed OHKOs Gengar, Archaludon Electro Shot guaranteed KOs Corviknight at 59%. Protecting only delays—opponent keeps double-attacking. Best shot is going aggressive: Shadow Ball+Brave Bird into Swampert (combined 52-91% vs 62% HP). If opponent double-targets Gengar to remove Shadow Tag, Corviknight survives and KOs Swampert with Brave Bird. Gengar outspeeds to chip first. Only path to stay alive.
decisions.notebook: G2 T6: Shadow Tag active, opponent trapped. Speed order: Gengar 200 > Archaludon 105-137 > Swampert 90-122 > Corviknight 87. Swampert HH guaranteed OHKOs Gengar. Archaludon Electro Shot guaranteed KOs Corviknight at 59% (124 min dmg > 121 remaining HP). Draco Meteor vs Gengar 74.5-107.3% possible KO. Shadow Ball+Brave Bird combined 52-91% vs Swampert 62% HP—can KO but not guaranteed. Opponent optimal: split targets for double KO. Our only chance: opponent double-targets Gengar, Corviknight survives to KO Swampert. If we survive with Corviknight alone vs Archaludon (-2 SpA from Draco Meteor), Electro Shot at -2 does ~27-39% (Corviknight survives). Series 0-1 down, must win G2+G3.

decisions.rationale: Without Rain, Corviknight (87-119) can outspeed Swampert (94) and double-target with Gengar to KO Swampert before it attacks. Switching Archaludon to Pelipper sets Rain immediately before moves resolve, boosting Swampert's Speed to 188 (outspeeding Corviknight). Swampert survives Gengar's Shadow Ball and OHKOs Gengar with High Horsepower. Under Rain, Archaludon can later OHKO Corviknight with Electro Shot.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent Gengar-Mega (Timid) + Corviknight (Careful, Leftovers) active. Swampert High Horsepower OHKOs Gengar-Mega. Archaludon Electro Shot OHKOs Corviknight in Rain.

decisions.rationale: Shadow Tag prevents switching. Double-targeting Mega Gengar with High Horsepower and Flash Cannon guarantees a KO through 100% accurate moves (even on a minimum damage roll, 98.2% + 32.3% > 100%), removing Shadow Tag and eliminating the opponent's primary offensive threat.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega has Shadow Tag trapping non-Ghosts. High Horsepower + Flash Cannon guarantees KO on Gengar-Mega.

decisions.rationale: Switching in Pelipper activates Drizzle rain. In rain, Archaludon's Electro Shot executes in a single turn, dealing 66.3-120.2% to Corviknight, which guarantees a KO on Corviknight's remaining 61% HP and wins Game 2.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Won to tie series 1-1. Corviknight finished by Archaludon's Drizzle-boosted Electro Shot after Gengar-Mega fainted to High Horsepower + Flash Cannon.

decisions.rationale: Gengar fainted, leaving only Corviknight (61%) vs 5 foe Pokémon including Archaludon (Electro Shot SE), Heliolisk (Electric SE), and Tsareena. No win condition exists at 1v5. Forfeiting G2 to conserve focus for G3 is the only rational play; continuing wastes time with zero realistic path to victory.
decisions.notebook: Series 0-1 down, lost G2. Must win G3 to force rubber match. Opponent team: Swampert-Mega (Adamant, Swampertite), Pelipper (Modest, Focus Sash consumed, Drizzle), Archaludon (Modest, Magnet, Stamina), Heliolisk (Timid, LifeOrb, DrySkin, 141-177 Spe), Tsareena (Adamant, MiracleSeed, QueenlyMajesty), Slowking-Galar (Bold, SitrusBerry, Regenerator). Opponent favors rain + Swampert-Mega + Archaludon core with Pelipper Tailwind support. Heliolisk outspeeds Mega Gengar (200) at max investment. For G3: prioritize speed control, keep Gengar healthy to trap key targets, avoid letting Swampert+Archaludon double-target for KOs. Klefki TWave support valuable vs fast rain team.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2, swept in two games. In Game 2, the four brought (Mega Gengar, Corviknight, Klefki, Conkeldurr) were poorly matched into the opponent's rain core. Klefki, brought for Thunder Wave support, was 2x weak to Swampert's Ground STAB and died immediately on turn 3 without providing lasting value. Conkeldurr was a liability — 4x weak to Flying, it was KO'd by Pelipper's Hurricane on turn 4 before doing meaningful damage. Mega Gengar entered too late, was outsped by rain-boosted Swampert-Mega, and got double-targeted down on turn 6. Corviknight was the only passable pick but couldn't output enough damage to swing the game. The opponent's Swampert-Mega + Archaludon + Pelipper rain engine overwhelmed a team with no Water resist, no speed control that stuck, and two Pokémon (Klefki, Conkeldurr) that were hard-weak to the opponent's main attacks.
reflections.adjustment: Register Toxapex over Conkeldurr or Klefki — Toxapex resists Water and Ice, walls Swampert-Mega with Recover/Haze, and survives Hurricane better than Conkeldurr survives anything. Reuniclus with Trick Room is also worth registering to reverse the opponent's speed tier entirely. If keeping Mega Gengar, pair it with speed control that isn't Ground-weak. Do not bring Conkeldurr into a rain + Hurricane team under any circumstances. Mamoswine and Gyarados, if brought, at least offer Ice Shard and Intimidate/Dragon Dance respectively — more useful than Conkeldurr's 4x Flying weakness. Consider whether Mega Gengar is even the right Mega here: its 200 Speed is outsped by rain Swampert-Mega and Heliolisk, and Shadow Tag trapping matters less when you can't survive to use it.
reflections.notebook: Opponent runs rain: Pelipper (Drizzle, Focus Sash, Modest, Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect) + Swampert-Mega (Adamant, High Horsepower/Liquidation/Ice Punch/Protect, outspeeds Mega Gengar in rain) + Archaludon (Modest, Magnet, Stamina, Electro Shot/Flash Cannon/Draco Meteor/Protect — Electro Shot charges and boosts SpA in rain). Also has Heliolisk (Timid, Life Orb, Dry Skin, Thunder/Weather Ball/Volt Switch/Electroweb — outspeeds Mega Gengar at 200), Tsareena (Adamant, Miracle Seed, Queenly Majesty, Trop Kick/HJK/U-turn/Protect), Slowking-Galar (Bold, Sitrus, Regenerator, Sludge Bomb/Psychic Noise/Chilly Reception/Protect). Opponent doubles aggressively, uses Tailwind for speed control, and exploits rain-boosted STAB. Key prep conclusions: (1) Toxapex is the single best answer from the full roster — resists Water/Ice, walls Swampert, punishes rain. (2) Conkeldurr is unbringable vs this team (4x Flying weak, outsped by everything relevant). (3) Klefki's Ground weakness and frailty make it unreliable speed control here. (4) Mega Gengar at 200 Spe is too slow for this matchup — consider an alternative Mega or commit to Trick Room/Thunder Wave before it enters. (5) Reuniclus Trick Room could flip the entire speed dynamic. (6) Opponent will protect Swampert and double-target the partner; plan around protecting your own partner accordingly.

reflections.summary: The 2-0 series victory was secured by a superior Rain core bringing Mega Swampert, Pelipper, Archaludon, and Tsareena. Evolving Mega Swampert was the optimal game plan: Swift Swim enabled it to outspeed Mega Gengar and hit high-value targets (Klefki, Gengar) with High Horsepower, while Pelipper eliminated Conkeldurr with Hurricane and Archaludon cleaned up with Electro Shot and Flash Cannon. Registration choices were spot-on, as the offensive Rain package overwhelmed the opponent's Klefki/Corviknight/Gengar core, making benching Garganacl, Mimikyu, Armarouge, and Scrafty correct.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, keep trusting the Rain core against their Klefki/Corviknight/Gengar structure, but prepare for potential counter-adjustments like Intimidate Gyarados or Focus Sash Mamoswine by bringing Heliolisk over Tsareena when secondary electric coverage is required.
reflections.notebook: Opponent heavily relies on a Prankster Klefki lead to inflict status and set screens, pairing it with bulky physical pivots (Corviknight, Conkeldurr) and Mega Gengar. Mega Swampert under Rain trivializes their speed control, while Archaludon handles Corviknight and residual threats under Drizzle. Queenly Majesty (Tsareena) effectively shuts down Prankster status and Conkeldurr's Mach Punch.
